sources.title: Implementation Issues for Superinstructions in Gforth
sources.paraphrase: Combining primitives can reduce dispatch; static and dynamic forms have implementation and tooling costs. The reported Forth performance is not evidence for this FP64 VM.

sources.title: Interpreters vs. Compiler Performance at Run-Time
sources.paraphrase: Stack caching, superinstructions and IP updates address different costs; interpreter/JIT categories alone do not determine performance. Microarchitectural pitfalls and implementation complexity matter. Forth reciprocal transforms do not preserve this project's FP64 contract.

sources.title: The Performance Effects of Virtual-Machine Instruction Pointer Updates
sources.read_via: publisher primary page and author paper reference
sources.paraphrase: Instruction-pointer update organization is a distinct interpreter optimization direction; this repository needs its own dependency-preserving evaluation.

sources.title: ORC Design and Implementation
sources.paraphrase: ORC supplies LLVM IR compilation and object linking layers, including COFF support. A JIT would require additional runtime/build integration and separate compilation-cost accounting.

sources.title: Clang Compiler User's Manual, Floating Point Model
sources.paraphrase: Disabling fast math alone can leave contraction enabled. Explicit -ffp-contract=off is needed here to preserve separately rounded multiply/add; signed zero and denormal behavior must remain intact.

repository_code_observation.current_dispatch: Each original operation updates last_pc/steps, copies a decoded record, advances pc and performs computed-goto dispatch; NEXT also checks intermediate stack size.
repository_code_observation.inference_not_measured: Control-flow-safe straight-line combinations or IP update changes could remove execution overhead while maintaining original operation boundaries. Static opcode frequency is not dynamic hotness.
